Hot spots and how long they last

Source: R/hotspot.R
hotpers.Rd

Counts incidents (break-ins, shootings, calls for service) in square grid cells for each period, measures how concentrated they are, picks out the hot cells of each period and says how much the hot set of one period overlaps the next. A hot spot that persists is a place problem; one that moves from period to period is not, and the two call for different responses.

Usage

hotpers(lon, lat, prd, cell = 0.25, top = 0.05, xy = c("lonlat", "planar"))

Arguments

lon, lat

Incident coordinates: longitude and latitude in degrees, or planar coordinates with coords = "planar".

prd

The period of each incident (a year, a month, a date, a label such as "Q1"); periods are taken in sorted order.

cell

Side of a grid cell: kilometres for longitude and latitude, map units otherwise; one positive number, default 0.25.

top

Share of the ever-active cells counted as hot in each period, in (0, 1]; default 0.05 (the busiest 5%).

xy

"lonlat" (the default, degrees) or "planar" (projected coordinates, such as metres in a UTM zone).

Value

An object of class rmbl_hotspot, a list:

periods

data frame, one row per period: period (character), incidents, actcells, cellsforhalf (fewest cells holding half the incidents), shrforhalf (that number over the ever-active cells), hotcells, tiedin (the cells made hot only by a tie with the k-th busiest), tiedout (the tied cells left out when the tie would have made more than twice k cells hot, which printing says), hotshr (share of the incidents in hot cells) and jacpre (NA for the first period). Shares are proportions in \([0, 1]\).

cells

data frame, one row per ever-active cell: x, y (its centre in the input's units), incidents and perhot.

cell, top, coords

the settings.

ncells, hotk

the number of ever-active cells and \(k\).

Details

Counts incidents in square cells of side cell (kilometres for longitude and latitude, map units otherwise) for each period and reports, per period: the incidents, the cells with any, the share of the ever-active cells that holds half the incidents (the law of crime concentration: a small share of places holds half the incidents), the hot cells (the top share of the ever-active cells with the most incidents, with the cells tied at the cut included unless the tie would more than double the hot set) and their share of the incidents, and the Jaccard overlap of the hot set with the previous period's (shared hot cells over cells hot in either). Per cell: the incidents in all, and in how many periods it was hot.

The ever-active cells (a cell with at least one incident in some period) are the base for the shares, so the empty land and water inside a city's bounding box do not dilute the concentration. The number of hot cells per period is \(k = \max(1, \lceil top \times n_{cells} \rceil)\).

Longitude and latitude are projected onto a flat map through the median point (equirectangular, Earth radius 6371.0088 km), which is accurate for a city or region; a warning is given when the incidents span more than 2000 km. The grid starts at the smallest projected coordinate. Points at (0, 0), the raw exports' “no location”, are dropped with a message, as are incidents with a non-finite coordinate or a missing period; longitudes across the antimeridian are taken on one side of it. When a tie empties a period's hot set, its overlap with the neighbouring periods is NA, not 0. The plot method draws the concentration, the overlap and a map of the cells.

Errors: lon, lat and prd of different lengths; cell not one positive number; top not in (0, 1]; coordinates outside the degree ranges with coords = "lonlat"; fewer than two usable incidents.

Examples

b <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "tps_break_enter_d14_2024.csv",
                          package = "rmoriebricklayer"))
b <- b[!is.na(b$lon), ]
q <- quarters(as.Date(b$occ_date))
h <- hotpers(b$lon, b$lat, q, cell = 0.3)
h$periods
#>   period incidents actcells cellsforhalf shrforhalf hotcells tiedin tiedout
#> 1     Q1       128       77           22  0.1582734       11      4       0
#> 2     Q2       133       74           22  0.1582734        7      0       0
#> 3     Q3       112       70           19  0.1366906        7      0       0
#> 4     Q4       135       72           23  0.1654676        4      0      12
#>      hotshr    jacpre
#> 1 0.3281250        NA
#> 2 0.2255639 0.2857143
#> 3 0.2678571 0.1666667
#> 4 0.1333333 0.1000000
plot(h)


# the cells hot in every quarter
subset(h$cells, perhot == 4)
#> [1] x         y         incidents perhot   
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)

# larger cells and a wider hot set
h2 <- hotpers(b$lon, b$lat, q, cell = 0.5, top = 0.1)
h2$periods[, c("period", "hotcells", "hotshr", "jacpre")]
#>   period hotcells    hotshr    jacpre
#> 1     Q1       11 0.4687500        NA
#> 2     Q2       14 0.5187970 0.3157895
#> 3     Q3        9 0.4196429 0.3529412
#> 4     Q4        7 0.3407407 0.3333333

# planar coordinates, here in kilometres
set.seed(3)
hotpers(stats::runif(200, 0, 10), stats::runif(200, 0, 10),
                    rep(2023:2024, 100), cell = 2, top = 0.2, xy = "planar")
#> ╭── Hot spots ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Active cells             25                                             │
#> │   Cell side                2 units                                        │
#> │   Periods                  2                                              │
#> │   Hot cells                the busiest 5 (20%)                            │
#> │   Hot in half the periods  8                                              │
#> │                                                                           │
#> │   By period                                                               │
#> │   period  incidents  actcells  cellsforhalf  shrforhalf  hotcells  tiedin │
#> │   ------  ---------  --------  ------------  ----------  --------  ------ │
#> │   2023          100        25             9  36.0%              4       0 │
#> │   2024          100        24             9  36.0%              5       0 │
#> │                                                                           │
#> │   period  tiedout  hotshr  jacpre                                         │
#> │   ------  -------  ------  ------                                         │
#> │   2023          8  26.0%                                                  │
#> │   2024          0  33.0%   0.1250                                         │
#> │                                                                           │
#> │   The busiest 5 cells hold 26.0% to 33.0% of a period's incidents.        │
#> │   Their overlap with the period before averages 0.125: the hot set is     │
#> │   mostly new each period, so these spots do not persist. 8 cells are      │
#> │   hot in at least half the periods.                                       │
#> │                                                                           │
#> │   shrforhalf is the share of active cells that hold half the incidents,   │
#> │   hotshr the share of incidents in the hot cells, and jacpre the          │
#> │   overlap of the hot cells with the period before (1 = the same cells).   │
#> │   Cells tied with the busiest 5 were left out of the hot set: the         │
#> │   counts are too even (or the cells too small) to single out hot spots.   │
#> │   period 2023: 8 cells tied                                               │
#> ╰───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

# a share of zero hot cells is refused
try(hotpers(b$lon, b$lat, q, top = 0))
#> Error : `top` must be a share in (0, 1]
